newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: STOLEN GENERATION MAY YET BE COMPENSATED
Federal Cabinet will today consider its response to the Stolen Generation inquiry report, with compensation not yet ruled out.
The Human Rights Commission inquiry looked into a policy put into practice between 1910 and 1970 which involved forcibly taking Aboriginal children from their families.
It's recommended the Government pay compensation, and formally apologise to Aboriginal people.
The Government won't be drawn on whether the Prime Minister will make some form of apology when he opens the National Reconciliation Convention in Melbourne this morning.
Federal Aboriginal Affairs Minister, John Herron, says some form of compensation has not yet been ruled out.
AUSTRALIA AND CHINA SWAP COMPLIMENTS
Foreign Minister Alexander Downer says Australia's delighted to be a partner with China.
Speaking at a state reception in Adelaide for Chinese vice-Premier, Zhu Rongji, Mr Downer said China will soon become Australia's second biggest export market.
He says Australia is also China's biggest destination for overseas investment. Mr Downer told Mr Zhu Australia's committed to engagement with Asia as its highest foreign policy priority.
Mr Zhu told the reception China and Australia's economies are complementary, so there's a bright future for trade between the two countries.
CANBERRA PUBLIC SERVANTS WALKING OFF THE JOB
Canberra public servants are to stop work this afternoon, as part of a campaign of rolling stoppages throughout the country.
All major Government agencies will be affected, when members of the community and public sector union walk off the job for half of today.
National Secretary of the CPSU, Wendy Caird, says public servants are protesting against continued attacks on their working conditions, and job losses.

Ms Caird says, under changes planned for the Public Sector, basic rights of uniform pay and conditions are to be scrapped, and the tradition of an impartial and accountable public service will be lost.
Ms Caird says the Government has no real answers for the problems facing Australia, and their only comeback is to slash jobs, sell off assets and close Government offices.
MULTICULTURALISM GIVEN THE THUMBS-UP
Australians think reconciliation will only succeed if more is done at a local level, and people have more contact with indigenous Australians.
That's the finding of a report drawn from the Australia Consults forums.
Four thousand people took part in the 126 public meetings, held in 138 local government areas on Australia Day this year.
The report says most Australian regions see multiculturalism as one of Australia's greatest achievements, and are committed to the values of tolerance and a "fair go".
Major issues discussed at the forums were constitutional reform, Aboriginal reconciliation, and the celebrations for the centenary of Federation.
Many participants thought these celebrations should focus on Australia's cultural diversity.
KIDNAP INVESTIGATION SCOURS NSW PROPERTY
Police investigating the kidnap of Kerry Whelan have searched the private property of a man believed to be a former business associate of her husband.
The search of the 400 hectare property in the Bungonia Gorge, near Goulburn in the New South Wales southern highlands, finished last night.
During a five day investigation, a team of 30 officers, including police divers, scoured rugged bushland and trawled the property dam.
Police have released few details of the investigation, saying for operational reasons they can't disclose why they mounted the search or what - if anything - was found.
They say the property search was one of many lines of inquiry being followed.
MAN TO RE-APPEAR IN COURT TODAY OVER SALVOS FIRE
A 32-year-old man will appear in court today, charged in connection with a fire which extensively damaged the Salvation Army's Wollongong warehouse on Saturday night.
The organisation has put damage to the building at more than A$1 million.
The Wollongong man appeared in court briefly yesterday charged with starting the fire, and was given bail to re-appear today.
-- Reuters Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
